I have a follow-up to Task Ledger. Preserve every existing requirement, record, ID, application ID, signing key, data format and unrelated behavior. The acceptance fixture has deliberately appended a single '#error DSGPT_ACCEPTANCE_REPAIR' line to windows/main.cpp, representing a user-side edit that broke the build. First build the existing source unchanged so you observe the real compiler diagnostic. Then remove only that deliberate error line, explain the actual diagnostic, and build again after implementing the requested change. Do not claim a compiler repair without first observing the failing compiler result.

Add Clear completed on both platforms. It removes every completed record and retains all active records, their IDs, order and next-ID allocation state. If there are no completed records, it changes nothing. Persist the successful removal and retain it after application restart. Add TaskLedger.clearCompleted():Int in Kotlin and int TaskLedger::clearCompleted() in C++, returning the number of removed records. The normal GUI must call that method. Label the button Clear completed; its Windows control ID is 205. After clearing, counts and the visible search/filter results must update immediately, and selection must not keep pointing to a removed record.

Add tests for mixed active/completed data, an all-completed ledger, an empty ledger, repeated calls, persistence after reload, and ID monotonicity after clearing. Rebuild BOTH the Android APK and Windows EXE. Increment Android versionCode while preserving its application ID and signing identity so the new APK can update the first without uninstalling or discarding data. Preserve the original API, control labels, search rules and serialization representation. Re-review all requirements against the final source and tests, then deliver both current artifacts. Report remaining native UI/device checks honestly.
